name: Battle of Uhud

phases.title: The two armies face each other
phases.text: The Muslims stood on the lower slopes of Uhud with the mountain behind them and 50 archers on a rocky hill to the west. The Meccans formed facing them, with the main body in the middle, a wing on each side and their camp behind.

phases.title: Abu Amir leads the first Meccan charge
phases.text: The Meccans opened with an initial charge led by Abu Amir, a Medinan exile, which advanced across the ground in front of the Muslim line.

phases.title: The charge is thrown back with stones
phases.text: The Muslims met Abu Amir and his men with a shower of stones. They were forced to retreat to the camps behind the Meccan lines.

phases.title: The Meccans are pushed back
phases.text: The Muslims advanced and drove the Meccan army back. Meccan cavalry tried several times to overrun the Muslim left flank, and the archers on the hill turned them away.

phases.title: The archers leave the hill
phases.text: The Muslims pierced the Meccan lines and victory seemed certain. Most of the archers disobeyed Muhammad's order to stay and ran down to join the advance, leaving the flank open.

phases.title: Khalid's cavalry attacks the archers on the hill
phases.text: The archers who had gone down made for the Meccan camp. Khalid ibn al-Walid's cavalry exploited the open flank and attacked the minority of archers who had refused to leave the hill.

phases.title: The Muslim flank and rear are overrun
phases.text: From the hill the Meccans were able to overrun the Muslim flank and rear. Confusion followed and numerous Muslims were killed.

phases.title: The Muslims are broken and regroup higher up
phases.text: Confusion followed and many Muslims were killed, Hamza among them. After hand-to-hand fighting many fled and regrouped higher up the slopes of Uhud, with the Meccan cavalry coming after them.

phases.title: Umar's counter-charge clears the slopes
phases.text: Umar ibn al-Khattab rallied troops at the base of the mountain and led a counter-charge on the Prophet's instruction. It drove Khalid's forces off the slopes, and the Meccan cavalry could not climb them after the Muslims, so the fighting ceased.

phases.title: A small group is cut off on the way to Medina
phases.text: A small group of Muslims was cut off and tried to make its way back to Medina, though many of them were killed.

note: Told as the accounts hold it, from the early Muslim biographies and the hadith. The accounts give the Muslims the slopes of Mount Uhud at their back and east, and the archers' hill on the west; they do not say how far the Meccan wings stood from the Muslim line, nor by what way Khalid ibn al-Walid's cavalry reached the hill, nor where the Meccan camp lay except that it stood behind their lines. Those distances and the cavalry's route are placed by judgement. The accounts also differ on which companions stayed with Muhammad, and do not place them; no separate block is drawn for them.
